items.stem: A month-end schedule must foot exactly to the penny, but the total shows a 0.01 difference. What is the most appropriate fix?

options.text: Apply ROUND to the calculated values at the defined precision so displayed and underlying figures agree
options.rationale: Correct: rounding the underlying values removes sub-cent floating-point residue so the schedule ties.

options.text: Manually type the correct total over the formula
options.rationale: Overtyping the formula breaks the audit trail and will silently go wrong next period.

options.text: Widen the column so more decimals show
options.rationale: Showing more decimals reveals the difference but does not make the schedule foot.

options.text: Delete the rows that cause the mismatch
options.rationale: Removing data to force a tie misstates the figures.

items.explanation: Correct: rounding the underlying values removes sub-cent floating-point residue so the schedule ties.

items.stem: Which practices strengthen the integrity of an accounting workbook? (Select TWO)

options.text: Separate input cells from formula cells and protect the formulas
options.rationale: Correct: isolating and locking formulas prevents accidental overwrites while leaving inputs editable.

options.text: Add independent check cells that flag when a statement does not tie
options.rationale: Correct: built-in checks catch errors before the report is relied upon.

options.text: Hard-code totals once they look right to speed up refresh
options.rationale: Hard-coded totals stop updating and hide later errors.

options.text: Keep all versions in one file by overwriting it each month
options.rationale: Overwriting destroys the audit trail and the ability to compare periods.

items.explanation: Correct: isolating and locking formulas prevents accidental overwrites while leaving inputs editable.; Correct: built-in checks catch errors before the report is relied upon.

items.stem: Why map each trial-balance account to a financial-statement line with a lookup that flags unmapped accounts?

options.text: New or renamed accounts are caught instead of being silently omitted from the statements
options.rationale: Correct: a flag on unmapped accounts surfaces gaps so nothing drops out of the report unnoticed.

options.text: It makes the workbook calculate faster
options.rationale: Speed is not the reason; completeness and control are.

options.text: It removes the need to reconcile at all
options.rationale: Mapping supports reporting but does not replace reconciliation.

options.text: It converts the accounts to cash basis automatically
options.rationale: Mapping assigns lines; it does not change the accounting basis.

items.explanation: Correct: a flag on unmapped accounts surfaces gaps so nothing drops out of the report unnoticed.
